svg.aria-label: Side-by-side contrast between a Receipts and Payments Account (Cash Basis) and an Income and Expenditure Account (Accrual Basis)
svg.text: Receipts & Payments Account vs. Income & Expenditure Account
The #1 Non-Profit Exam Distinction: Receipts & Payments tracks ALL CASH (Capital + Revenue); Income & Expenditure tracks ACCRUAL REVENUE ONLY!
Receipts & Payments A/c (Summary Cash Book)
Basis: STRICT CASH BASIS
• Starts with: Opening Cash / Bank Balance b/d
• Debit side: ALL Cash & Cheques RECEIVED
• Credit side: ALL Cash & Cheques PAID OUT
• Includes BOTH Capital & Revenue items!
(e.g. buying new gym equipment $5,000 IS included!)
• Ignores accruals, prepayments & depreciation!
• Includes cash received for LAST yr & NEXT yr
Ends With: Closing Cash / Bank Balance c/d
(Does NOT show whether club made a Surplus or Deficit!)
Income & Expenditure A/c (Club Income Stmt)
Basis: STRICT ACCRUAL & MATCHING BASIS
• NO Opening or Closing Cash/Bank Balances!
• Includes ONLY THIS YEAR'S Revenue Income
• Includes ONLY THIS YEAR'S Revenue Expenses
• EXCLUDES Capital Expenditure & Capital Receipts!
(Buying $5,000 equipment → Balance Sheet Asset!)
• INCLUDES Accruals, Prepayments & Depreciation!
• Includes Net Bar / Dance Profit (or Loss)
Ends With: SURPLUS or DEFICIT for the Year
(Transferred directly to Accumulated Fund on Bal Sheet!)
Watch Out: In a Receipts & Payments A/c, Receipts sit on DEBIT & Payments on CREDIT — identical to a Cash Book!
